identity.title: ShEPhERD: Diffusing shape, electrostatics, and pharmacophores for bioisosteric drug design

problem.claim: Design bioisosteric or related drug analogues with precise 3D interaction profiles by generating molecules conditioned on shape, electrostatics, and pharmacophores.

contributions.claim: ShEPhERD: an SE(3)-equivariant diffusion model that jointly denoises 3D molecular graphs and representations of shape, electrostatic potential surfaces, and directional pharmacophores.
A composition of 3D similarity scoring functions for assessing conditional generation against desired interaction profiles.
Demonstrations on natural-product ligand hopping, protein-blind bioactive-hit diversification, and bioisosteric fragment merging.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors propose learning the joint distribution of 3D molecular structures and interaction profiles through joint diffusion of both molecule and interaction representations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report demonstrating ShEPhERD’s potential through three exemplary drug-design tasks: natural-product ligand hopping, protein-blind bioactive-hit diversification, and bioisosteric fragment merging.
The authors report using composed 3D similarity scores to assess conditional generation of novel molecules with desired interaction profiles.

narrative_sequence.summary: Chemical design is framed around engineering precise 3D intermolecular interactions.
Bioisosteric analogues are commonly sought by virtual screening with shape, electrostatic, and pharmacophore similarity scores.
The authors hypothesize that joint modeling of 3D structures and interaction profiles can support interaction-aware design, and instantiate this in ShEPhERD.
They compose similarity scores for conditional-generation assessment and report application demonstrations across three drug-design tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a conventional screening representation—shape, electrostatics, and pharmacophores—to both the model’s denoised outputs and its assessment scores.

lessons.interpretation: Reusing task-relevant representations across modeling and evaluation can make the intended design objective easier to track.
lessons.application: Define the target interaction descriptors before modeling, expose them as controllable outputs, and evaluate generated candidates with aligned descriptor-level scores.
lessons.exception: This alignment may be unsuitable when the descriptors omit important biological or chemical constraints not represented by the scoring functions.

unknowns: The abstract does not report numerical results, baselines, dataset details, or the conditions under which the three demonstrations succeed.
It does not specify whether the proposed joint model outperforms virtual screening or other generative approaches.
